title: Akamai current decision desk
status: Material demand signal · execution economics unresolved
purpose: Akamai's expanded Anthropic relationship materially strengthens the evidence for cloud-infrastructure demand. It does not yet establish revenue timing, gross margin, cash return, realized dilution, or an expectation gap.

currentDecision.label: Decision today
currentDecision.detail: Treat the announcement as a stronger demand signal, not a reason to change the scenario model or make an investment conclusion. The next decision turns on deployment, revenue conversion, capacity economics, and the warrant's effect.

facts.label: Contracted commitment
facts.detail: Akamai disclosed a contractual Anthropic commitment, with potential for about $9B more. Contract value is not recognized revenue.

facts.label: FY2026 revenue guide
facts.detail: Akamai said the agreement does not change its FY2026 revenue guidance.

facts.label: Capacity burden
facts.detail: Akamai estimates about $1.7B of incremental 2026 capital investment to secure and pre-purchase memory and related components.

facts.label: Warrant structure
facts.detail: The current commitment is associated with about 2% of common stock on an as-converted basis; further vesting depends on expansion of the relationship.

nextQuestions.title: When does it become revenue?
nextQuestions.detail: Look for deployment milestones, revenue-recognition timing, remaining-performance-obligation or backlog disclosure, and the first reported contribution.

nextQuestions.title: What are the unit economics?
nextQuestions.detail: Look for price, gross-margin, cost-to-serve, capacity utilization, and duration information—not just another contract headline.

nextQuestions.title: Can Akamai fund it well?
nextQuestions.detail: Test capex, operating cash flow, free-cash-flow conversion, financing needs, and margin guidance against the added capacity burden.

nextQuestions.title: What is the concentration and warrant cost?
nextQuestions.detail: Clarify customer concentration, service and supply-chain dependencies, warrant accounting and vesting, and any actual share-count effect.

boundary: A signed commitment proves a customer and creates an obligation. It does not by itself prove recognized revenue, attractive gross margin, cash returns, realized dilution, or that market expectations are too low.
sourceNote: All figures in this decision desk are from Akamai's September 24, 2026 company announcement. The dashboard preserves the contract-versus-revenue distinction and leaves non-disclosed economics unresolved.
